title_ar: الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو يشارك في المؤتمر العام الثامن للحركة الإسلامية بالسودان
title_en: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew Takes Part in the Eighth General Conference of the Islamic Movement in Sudan
body_ar: شارك الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم على رأس وفد من جمعية المستقبل في المؤتمر العام الثامن للحركة الإسلامية السودانية، المنعقد في العاصمة الخرطوم في الفترة: من الأول إلى الثالث من محرم 1434هـ الموافق 15-17 نوفمبر 2012م، لمدة ثلاثة أيام في قاعة الصداقة بالخرطوم، وقد شارك الشيخ في الجلسة الثانية من المؤتمر في اليوم الأول بتقديم مداخلة حول "الإسلاميون والآخر". حضر جلسات المؤتمر نحو أربعة آلاف عضو من الرجال والنساء والشباب يمثلون ولايات السودان كافة وقطاعات المجتمع الفاعلة. شرف المؤتمر حضور عالمي كثيف من قيادات الحركات الإسلامية العليا يمثلون أكثر من ثلاثين دولة بينها دول عربية شقيقة وإسلامية صديقة. وأكد المؤتمر في بيانه الختامي وقوف الحركة مع حق الشعب الفلسطيني ودعا لوقف نزيف الدم السوري كما دعا إلى تكثيف الحوار بين الحركات الإسلامية . ودعا المؤتمر منظمة التعاون الإسلامي للعمل على وقف المذابح ضد المسلمين في ماينمار. وسينشر الموقع – بإذن الله – مشاركة الشيخ الددو في المؤتمر في وقت لاحق.
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew — president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars and president of the Future Association for Calling to Islam, Culture and Education — took part, at the head of a delegation from the Future Association, in the Eighth General Conference of the Sudanese Islamic Movement, convened in the capital, Khartoum, in the period from the first to the third of Muharram 1434 AH, corresponding to 15–17 November 2012, over three days in the Friendship Hall in Khartoum. The Sheikh took part in the conference's second session, on the first day, by giving an intervention on "The Islamists and the Other".

The conference's sessions were attended by some four thousand members — men, women and young people — representing all the states of Sudan and the active sectors of society. The conference was honoured by a heavy international attendance of the senior leaderships of the Islamic movements, representing more than thirty states, among them fraternal Arab states and friendly Muslim ones.

In its closing statement the conference affirmed the movement's standing with the right of the Palestinian people, and called for a halt to the haemorrhage of Syrian blood, as it also called for the intensifying of dialogue among the Islamic movements. The conference called upon the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation to work towards a halt to the massacres against Muslims in Myanmar.

The site will, God permitting, publish Sheikh al-Dedew's contribution to the conference at a later date.

flags.arabic: المؤتمر العام الثامن للحركة الإسلامية السودانية
flags.context: the body whose conference the Sheikh addressed, at the head of a delegation
options: translate faithfully and refer the publication decision upward
translate and publish as ordinary content
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, style guide section 12. The Sudanese Islamic Movement was the ideological organisation of the governing order in Sudan in 2012, under a head of state then subject to an ICC arrest warrant; the conference was held in the same Friendship Hall as the human-rights conference of record 798, five months earlier, also under that government's auspices. The Sheikh attended at the head of his own association's delegation and addressed a session. The record contains no statement of his and no religious content, so what is at issue is purely association and how it reads in English a decade on. Nothing has been omitted or characterised beyond what the source says. The publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: the title of the Sheikh's intervention; no content is given
options: The Islamists and those who differ from them
flags.note: The subject is how Islamist movements should relate to those outside them — non-Muslims, secular opponents, other currents — which is precisely the question the Sheikh addressed from a different angle in record 796 ('Loyalty and Disavowal and Its Role in Entrenching Citizenship'). The corpus holds the title and nothing else in both cases. 'الآخر' is the Other in the sense used in modern Arabic intellectual writing, and the definite singular is kept rather than resolved into a list. The site's closing promise to publish his contribution should be checked against the corpus.

options: the massacres against Muslims in Myanmar
the killings of Muslims in Myanmar
the slaughter of Muslims in Burma
flags.note: The reference is to the violence in Rakhine State in 2012. مذابح is 'massacres' and that force is kept; nothing has been softened. Note that this is the conference's resolution, not a statement by the Sheikh, and the English keeps the subject as 'the conference' throughout the paragraph. The source spells Myanmar ماينمار.

options: fraternal Arab states and friendly Muslim ones
sister Arab countries and friendly Islamic countries
Arab brother states and allied Muslim states
flags.note: A fixed pairing of Arab diplomatic and party language — Arab states are 'fraternal', non-Arab Muslim states are 'friendly' — encoding a distinction of degree that English does not naturally make. Rendered literally rather than flattened to 'other countries', because the distinction is the point of the phrase.

translator_notes: A news-desk report of a party conference, closely following the conference's own communiqué in its third paragraph. It carries no words of the Sheikh's.
The CMS timestamp, 18 November 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the conference ran 1–3 Muharram 1434 / 15–17 November 2012.
'الإسلاميون' is rendered 'the Islamists', the standard English for the political current, as against 'Muslims' for المسلمون; the source keeps the two distinct and so does the English.
'منظمة التعاون الإسلامي' is the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, in the English form the body uses itself.
